messages:
incidents-bot: Paging: P1 incident -> HeliosPharm (dedicated pool) high tail latency detected, alert at 2026-03-15T02:14:00Z. Symptoms: p95 generation latency > 2s, error rate creeping 0.7%.

maria: saw it. I'm oncall. digging into tenant queue metrics now.

aj: tagging in. is HeliosPharm on bespoke shaper?

maria: yes, they're on dedicated pool `ded-pool-12` with bespoke shaper + reduced max_batch_tokens (256) historically. Metrics show burst at 02:12 UTC.

kevin: quick summary of what I see from runtime: sustained enqueue depth jumped from ~30 -> 220 over 3m, scheduler started dropping into tail-shed after 180. KV cache hits unchanged.

maria: thanks. can we reduce per-tenant max inflight until we stabilize? suggestion: set tenant.shed_threshold=120 and tenant.max_batch_tokens=128 as temporary.

tamsin: +1 to lowering max_batch_tokens — smaller batches reduce head-of-line blocking for this workload. but watch cost implications.

aj: preparing a canary change. plan: apply to HeliosPharm only for 10m, monitor p95 and throughput. command:
```bash
shaperctl apply --tenant heliospharm --set "max_batch_tokens=128" --set "shed_threshold=120" --duration 10m --reason "emergency tail latency mitigation"
```

lia: can you also temporarily bump routing fallback to allow requests to route to compat-llama-medium if latency doesn't improve? that's a last-resort fallback.

maria: agree but want to try in-pool knobs first. executing canary now.

incidents-bot: Action logged: `shaperctl apply` by maria at 02:18:14Z. Change ID: shaper-4750001234-1.

kevin: canary live. I'm watching the queue depth and per-GPU utilization. current p95 generation = 2.18s, p99 = 3.9s.

maria: after 90s: p95 -> 1.02s, p99 -> 1.8s. enqueue depth down to ~70.

aj: nice. throughput dipped ~8% but error rate stable. CPU/GPU utilization per-pod small drop.

tamsin: any sign of request-starvation (clients timing out)? we need to ensure we didn't mask correctness.

lia: customer support pinged HeliosPharm. no reported errors from them yet. their SDK retries might increase QPS — watch for retry storms.

kevin: rolling this to full tenant (not global) now. applying permanent: `max_batch_tokens=128`, `shed_threshold=110`, `scheduler_weight=0.85` for HeliosPharm. CLI: 
```bash
shaperctl apply --tenant heliospharm --set "max_batch_tokens=128" --set "shed_threshold=110" --set "scheduler_weight=0.85" --reason "stabilize burst queues"
```

maria: deployed. metrics after 3m: p95 950ms, p99 1.6s, enqueue depth ~55.

aj: added a temporary autoscale rule to increase pool capacity if queue depth > 150 for > 2m: `autoscaler.attach --pool ded-pool-12 --policy burst-2x-5m`

incidents-bot: Autoscaler policy attached by aj at 02:26:40Z.

tamsin: can we tweak tenant-level prefix cache window? this workload looks repetitive — caching prefixes could cut tokens.

kevin: good idea. set prefix_cache.ttl=60s for this tenant as an experiment. command: `rctl set tenant.heliospharm.prefix_cache_ttl 60`

maria: applied prefix cache 60s. immediate effect: repeated calls with same context drop token compute by ~22%.

lia: customer notified: "We've applied temporary performance knobs (shorter batches, caching) to reduce latency; will update when stable."

kevin: monitoring 10m now for regression. early signs good. no new 5xx seen, latency stable.

maria: postmortem note: root cause appears to be a combination of an upstream ingestion spike (customer-side burst) + a recent workload change that produced larger average response lengths which increased batch token budget. will follow up with HeliosPharm SRE for smoothing of client-side burst.

aj: follow-ups: 1) schedule a post-incident call with HeliosPharm engineering, 2) add a safety check in the scheduler to auto-lower max_batch_tokens when per-tenant enqueue depth > 150, 3) add a dashboard tile for bespoke-tenant queue depth SLOs.

maria: assigning action items: aj -> post-incident call; tamsin -> scheduler auto-lowering RFC; kevin -> validate prefix cache safety for structured prompts; lia -> customer comms + do they want traffic shaping on their side.

incidents-bot: Incident resolved for HeliosPharm at 02:35:50Z. Summary: latency mitigated by dynamic shaper changes, prefix caching, and autoscaler policy. Severity downgraded.

maria: closing oncall handoff in 10m. leaving notes in oncall runbook. great quick team work :thumbsup:

aj: adding a short-lived alert to remind us to revert non-permanent costy knobs in 24h.

kevin: will run an eval to ensure generation quality unchanged with smaller batches — will post results in #eng-runtime later.

maria: thanks all, handing off to aj for monitoring window. we can close thread after 24h or after postmortem posted.

aj: acknowledged, taking over monitoring.
